US stocks have rarely been this oversold:

The S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, its widest deviation since August 2015.

This also marks its 3rd-largest deviation in at least 20 years.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, the index’s largest deviation from its 50-DMA was 3.6 standard deviations.

Not even the 2020 Pandemic crash saw such extreme oversold conditions, with the S&P 500 falling 3.8 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average in February.

During the 2022 bear market and the April 2025 post-"Liberation Day" selloff, the S&P 500 fell 3.2 and 3.3 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, respectively.

This has been one of the sharpest market sell-offs in history.

To give more context - as Fed intervention has historically been the main driver of V bottoms - my mental model of Warsh is that he is a highly ambitious man. He profoundly desired the Fed Chair seat and did whatever it took to get it. He is beholden to Trump, especially given his FIL's close relationship to Trump, and whatever promises that were made.

Yet when you consider his incentives from here, his #1 priority should be to get reappointed. Given the shift in political winds, it is highly likely this will be done by a Dem President. A Dem is highly unlikely to reappoint Warsh unless there is incontrovertible evidence that he is not a Trump stooge. What better way is there to ensure this than to get publicly criticized by Trump, and enter the hot seat, as Powell had done? And now Trump has suffered huge aura loss and is a lame duck. He can talk shit but not much else.

So either Warsh goes all out in rebuking Trump to elicit public criticism since it directly benefits his chances of reappointment, or he goes for a softer strategy based on his record, where he continues to thread the needle between being hawkish and blaming the rest of the committee in private conversations with Trump. In any case, the Fed put feels very far away. 

Another subtle clue is that in recent weeks, sell-side rates desks were convinced that the Fed would bring back RMPs in order to prevent another repo tightening episode given the continued heavy bills issuance putting pressure on bank reserves. There was compelling logic to do so, yet Warsh did not. It is clear he would rather let something break first than preemptively expand the balance sheet. So this is another case of Warsh following his own agenda versus doing something that would be aligned with Trump's goals.

The 2026 $BTC bottom is in! I think that was it, guys.  This is my official call!

$BTC back-tested the diagonal trend line ✅ and bounced with good volume✅.  

It has now recovered fully back above the $57.7k July low, reclaiming it as support! This means it was a SWING LOW, which can indicate a powerful reversal of the downtrend.

There was also confluence with the blue megaphone pattern as well ✅, so it seemed a likely place to offer some support, which added to my suspicion it could be a place for a bounce. We now have 3 touches of the lower boundary.

Just as the deviation (aka fake-out, aka swing HIGH) above the May high was followed by a powerful reversal downward, this deviation (aka fake-out, aka swing LOW) below the $57.7k July low is likely to be followed by a powerful reversal UPWARD.

Also, I believe the S&P500 reached a LOCAL LOW on Friday. It pushed deep into support and is oversold and likely for a short term bounce. It could see lower lows in several months (I'm not as certain that the stock low is in fully-- it may or may not be). But the rebound we'll likely see in stocks next week will help push BTC higher. A rising tide lifts all boats.

I’m willing to bet that was the final low. Do I know with 100% certainty? Of course not, because you can't ever know that with any market. But I strongly believe it was the final cycle bottom.

Very exciting!  Finally we can move onward and upward!
